readerFields.title: Food Technology

audience.programmeDescription: Food Technology at Wageningen applies chemistry, physics, microbiology and quantitative methods to food ingredients, production, safety, quality and product innovation. The English-taught bachelor combines laboratory work, industrial cases and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines molecular and laboratory science with product design, quantitative methods and circularity. The second studies eating behaviour and consumer responses; the third studies ecological and governance aspects of food systems. WUR has a more cumulative food-chemistry, microbiology, physics, preservation and process-engineering sequence.

componentTitles: BSc Thesis Food Science and Technology
programmeLabels: Ecology, circular resources & sustainable food systems
concepts: Combine cell biology, biochemistry and microbial laboratory methods with physiological foundations, mathematics and consumer-product research. Material experiments, life-cycle assessment, farming and circular-resource analysis connect product innovation to environmental consequences. This is a related route into sustainable food-product questions; it does not provide the cumulative food-chemistry, food-physics, preservation and process-engineering curriculum.

Investigate eating choices through physiology, biochemical energy handling, regulatory neurobiology, perception, social influence and health behaviour. Consumer research, product design, behavioural economics and communication connect those mechanisms to product acceptance and health messages. These are substantial scientific and research tools for the application, with no claim to a specialist nutrition, food-sensory-testing or manufacturing sequence.

Study the ecological and resource conditions of food production through biodiversity, farming, soils, water, climate and life-cycle assessment. Governance, economics, ethics and consumer-product design connect agricultural practices to environmental costs and collective choices. This is a food-systems application of environmental mechanisms and methods, with a direct farming anchor; it is not a food-manufacturing or food-engineering degree.

notes.text: Wageningen Food Technology provides a cumulative food-science and engineering curriculum, including food chemistry, microbiology, physics, preservation, processing, packaging and quality. These UCR programmes approach related questions through molecular and environmental science, eating behaviour and consumer research, or sustainable food systems. They do not reproduce that specialist food-technology sequence.

selectedCourseDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
selectedCourseDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
